item.title: Kinrox 0.5.0
item.description:
Spotify playback now runs directly on your Mac through Spotify Soloist, with Spotify.app fully closed. Requires an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 14 or later. Version 0.5.0, build 10.

Download Kinrox-0.5.0-arm64.dmg, open it, and drag Kinrox to Applications. Users of 0.3.0 or later can use Check for Updates. Video libraries are bundled; Homebrew and Xcode are not required.

Spotify setup

Spotify Premium, your own Spotify developer Client ID and a personal Soloist API key are required. Accept the updated connection terms in Settings, enter the key and download the engine directly from Spotify. Pair once using Spotify on iPhone on the same local network. After pairing, Spotify on both Mac and iPhone can be closed.

Soloist is downloaded separately and is not bundled or redistributed by Kinrox. Its builds expire after 90 days; Settings provides an engine update action. Keys stay in the Mac Keychain, but are passed to Soloist in process arguments readable by other programs under the same user account. The local playback socket has no authentication. The connection terms explain these limitations and cleanup.

Changes

  • Play, pause, seek, volume and track changes use the native engine. There is no Spotify.app or embedded browser fallback.
  • Kinrox owns the queue locally, including repeated tracks, shuffle and repeat. Playback no longer creates or rewrites a Spotify helper playlist; existing helper playlists remain untouched and excluded from bulk favorite changes.
  • After 20 seconds paused, the audio process stops. Play restores the saved position; recovery after a long pause typically takes 2–3 seconds.
  • iPhone controls remain on the encrypted local connection. The updated remote handles unknown volume and recovery states; App Store publication is separate.
  • Fixed video opening failing when the music engine had never started, and recovery after an audio process or its supervisor exited unexpectedly.
  • Improved recovery from interrupted engine setup, stale playback endpoints and externally resumed playback after a pause.
  • Setup and recovery screens, connection terms and privacy documents support all 30 application languages.

Verification and limitations

Live tests ran with Spotify.app absent. The owner confirmed audible playback. A 30-minute run measured Soloist at 24.73–27.30 MiB and about 1% of one CPU core. On a physical iPhone, 1,003 commands completed without failure; 200 Next samples had p95 3.095 seconds, within the owner-approved 3.2-second limit. The slowest Next in that run took 4.066 seconds. Cold/warm startup p95 was 2.93/2.23 seconds.

MP4/MKV rendering, audio-output changes, a brief network interruption and process crash recovery were verified. Physical Mac sleep and system reboot checks were waived by the owner for this release and remain untested. Runtime verification used macOS 26.5.2; macOS 14 is the deployment minimum, without a separate runtime check. These boundaries and automated results are recorded in Standalone Spotify Verification.

Kinrox-0.5.0-dependency-sources.tar.gz contains the bundled open-source dependency sources, build recipes and patches; it contains no Soloist binary or archive. Licenses are included in the app. SHA256SUMS.txt provides asset checksums; matching application source is available at tag v0.5.0 after publication.

item.title: Kinrox 0.4.2
item.description:
Welcome-screen layout fixes and faster Spotify library and playback controls. Requires an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Version 0.4.2, build 8.

Download Kinrox-0.4.2-arm64.dmg, open it, and drag Kinrox to Applications. All video playback libraries are bundled; Homebrew and Xcode are not required. Users of 0.3.0 or later can use Check for Updates.

Fixed

  • Recent files could widen the welcome screen beyond the window, pushing its heading, Open File button and Show all action off-screen. The grid now uses its actual column width, and the decorative glow no longer widens small windows.
  • A regression test checks empty, single-file and longer recent lists while shrinking and growing the same window between 640 and 1440 points.

Spotify improvements

  • A local SQLite metadata cache restores the library progressively and reduces repeated loading. It stores metadata only, expires unvalidated resources after seven days, is limited to 100 MiB, and is removed on disconnect.
  • Library indexing, shared requests and request priorities reduce repeated work and let playback controls take precedence over background library loading.
  • Resume and unchanged-order track changes avoid rewriting the private queue. Manual queue insertion preserves playback; paused edits do not start music.
  • A local clock advances playback progress. Kinrox checks after commands and at the expected track boundary instead of continuously polling Spotify.
  • Updated connection terms and privacy disclosures explain the cache in all 30 languages. Existing users must accept the new terms before reconnecting.

Spotify setup remains as described in the 0.4.0 release notes. Changes made directly in Spotify are observed on the next Kinrox command or expected track boundary. The companion iPhone app is released separately.

Compatibility and verification

The welcome-screen regression failed before the fix and passed afterward; rendered normal and narrow windows were inspected. The Mac suite passed with 220 tests in 44 suites using both development and portable release libraries. Music-package tests (36), protocol/transport tests (126), release-tooling tests (46), localization and generated-site checks also passed. Live Spotify and optional Music screenshot tests are opt-in and were not enabled.

The app and DMG passed Apple notarization. The mounted app passed signature, Gatekeeper, stapling and bundled-library verification. Its actual welcome screen, synthetic MP4/MKV playback, pause, seeking and fullscreen entry/exit were checked interactively with Kinrox volume set to zero. Automated tests cover secure remote pairing; no new interactive pairing check was performed.

Verification uses macOS 26.5.2. macOS 14 remains the deployment minimum; live Spotify playback and a physical iPhone have not been rechecked for this release. Detailed cache behavior, synthetic measurements and limitations are recorded in the performance report.

Kinrox-0.4.2-dependency-sources.tar.gz contains dependency sources, build recipes and patches. Licenses are included in the app. SHA256SUMS.txt provides asset checksums; matching application source is available at tag v0.4.2.

item.title: Kinrox 0.4.1
item.description:
Spotify playback reliability and fullscreen video fixes. Requires an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Version 0.4.1, build 7.

Download Kinrox-0.4.1-arm64.dmg, open it, and drag Kinrox to Applications. All video playback libraries are bundled; Homebrew and Xcode are not required. Users of 0.3.0 or later can use Check for Updates.

Fixed

  • A delayed Spotify poll response could overwrite the state of a completed playback command or stop further polling. Superseded responses and errors are now ignored; current playback failures still report normally.
  • Fullscreen video now fills the window without reserving space for the Video/Music mode picker. The picker returns when leaving fullscreen, preserving the video view.

Compatibility and verification

Spotify setup and features remain as described in the 0.4.0 release notes. The SQLite cache and playback-latency work is a reviewed implementation plan and is not included in this release. The companion iPhone app is released separately.

Release verification uses macOS 26.5.2. macOS 14 remains the deployment minimum; live Spotify playback and a physical iPhone have not been rechecked for this patch. The full Mac suite passed on rerun (183 tests; two intentionally skipped), alongside 27 music-package tests, 126 protocol/transport tests, and 45 release-tooling tests. The first Mac run encountered a Matrix transport disconnection; that suite passed in isolation and the subsequent full run passed. Localization and formatting checks also passed.

Both the app and DMG passed Apple notarization. The mounted app passed signature, Gatekeeper, stapling and bundled-library checks, and its welcome window opened. The additional interactive pairing/playback smoke check could not finish because the computer-use tool became unavailable. Automated Mac tests cover pairing, playback and the fullscreen layout regression.

Kinrox-0.4.1-dependency-sources.tar.gz contains dependency sources, build recipes and patches. Licenses are included in the app. SHA256SUMS.txt provides asset checksums; matching application source is available at tag v0.4.1.

item.title: Kinrox 0.4.0
item.description:
Spotify music mode, queue editing, favorites and localized connection documents. Requires an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Version 0.4.0, build 6.

Download Kinrox-0.4.0-arm64.dmg, open it, and drag Kinrox to Applications. All video playback libraries are bundled; Homebrew and Xcode are not required. Users of 0.3.0 can use Check for Updates. Earlier versions can install this DMG directly.

New

  • Music library with albums, tracks, catalogue search and a compact three-column view.
  • Track likes, saved albums and followed artists, with favorite undo and playlist options.
  • Editable queue with duplicate occurrences, shuffle, repeat, reordering and removal.
  • Official Spotify Connect playback through a private Kinrox Queue playlist.
  • Coordinated video/music playback and shared system media keys.
  • Music controls, queue and favorites through the encrypted iPhone LAN connection. These require a companion build containing music support; this release does not publish a new iPhone app to the App Store.
  • Spotify attribution, playback restrictions, recovery actions and bundled connection terms/privacy documents in all 30 supported app languages.
  • Updated component licensing and project information. The Mac remains GPL-3.0-only; new iPhone source revisions use the personal-use license described in LICENSING.md.

Spotify setup and behavior

Spotify is optional. It requires Spotify Premium, the official Spotify app on the same Mac, and your own Spotify developer app Client ID. Add http://127.0.0.1:43821/callback to that app's redirect URIs. Development Mode accounts must be allowed by that developer app.

In Kinrox Settings → Spotify, read and accept the connection terms, enter the public Client ID, then connect in your browser. No client secret is requested. Open Music with Command-2; Command-F searches and Command-R refreshes.

Audio plays in Spotify.app. Kinrox sends Spotify requests only from Mac; iPhone controls stay on the LAN, while user-activated Spotify links open externally. Credentials remain in the Mac Keychain. Disconnect clears local credentials and cache but leaves the helper playlist and intentional library edits in Spotify. Unliking a track removes its copies from editable playlists; Command-Z can undo the latest favorite action. Artist follows remain independent.

Read the connection terms and privacy policy before connecting.

Limits and verification

Spotify API polling can delay updates. Duplicate playlist occurrences cannot always be distinguished after external playback changes. No album artwork is shown. Spotify availability and developer-app access are controlled by Spotify; this release does not imply Spotify approval.

Runtime checks use macOS 26.5.2. macOS 14 and iOS 17 are deployment targets, not separately tested devices in this release session. Earlier physical-iPhone music checks are documented in Music Verification.

Kinrox-0.4.0-dependency-sources.tar.gz contains dependency sources, build recipes and patches. Licenses are included in the app. SHA256SUMS.txt provides asset checksums; matching application source is available at tag v0.4.0.

item.title: Kinrox 0.3.0
item.description:
Matrix screensaver, live folder playlists, and update reminders for Mac. Requires an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Version 0.3.0, build 5.

Download Kinrox-0.3.0-arm64.dmg, open it, and drag Kinrox to Applications. All playback libraries are bundled; Homebrew and Xcode are not required.

New

  • Matrix screensaver: choose Screensaver → Matrix. A playing movie pauses before the falling green code appears. Esc returns to the paused movie without leaving fullscreen. Matrix also works with no video open.
  • Live folder playlists: newly available videos appear in Next/Previous navigation without reopening the current file. Changes also reach the iPhone remote and system media controls. Playback position is preserved.
  • Update reminders: Kinrox checks for updates daily and offers a welcome-screen banner, a compact reminder while paused, and Check for Updates in the app menu. Sparkle verifies and installs updates when you choose to update.
  • Project links: the About panel and Help menu link to the website, source, license, support, issue tracker, and privacy policy.

Reliability

  • Matrix waits for the playback engine to confirm pause. Remote start requests report errors or cancellation instead of acknowledging an unconfirmed start.
  • Starting Matrix dismisses the Connect iPhone card; pairing cards retain Esc priority.
  • Folder watching recovers after directory replacement or temporary unavailability, and checks for new episodes at the end of playback.
  • Release startup verification leaves Sparkle's saved update preferences untouched.

Updating from 0.2.0

Versions 0.2.0 and earlier have no built-in updater. Install 0.3.0 manually once; subsequent releases can be offered inside the player.

Playback and remote commands stay on the local network. Update checks read an HTTPS feed on GitHub Pages without unique identifiers, system profiling, or telemetry. Installing an update downloads its signed DMG from GitHub Releases. See the privacy policy.

This is a Mac release. The iPhone App Store release is separate; Matrix remote controls require a companion build with the Screensavers section.

Runtime verification targets macOS 26.5.2. macOS 14 is the deployment target; a separate macOS 14 machine was not used for this release.

Kinrox-0.3.0-dependency-sources.tar.gz contains corresponding dependency sources, build recipes, and patches. Licenses are included inside the app. SHA256SUMS.txt provides release-asset checksums. The matching application source is available at the v0.3.0 tag.
